parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
A cylinder is suspended from the end of a string. The cylinder is stationary in water with the
axis of the cylinder vertical, as shown in Fig. 2.1.
The cylinder has weight 0.84 N, height h and a circular cross-section of diameter 0.031 m.
The density of the water is 1.0 × 10^{3} kg m^{-3}. The difference between the pressures on the top
and bottom faces of the cylinder is 520 Pa.
parts.question_text_latex:
A cylinder is suspended from the end of a string. The cylinder is stationary in water with the
axis of the cylinder vertical, as shown in Fig. 2.1.
The cylinder has weight 0.84 N, height h and a circular cross-section of diameter 0.031 m.
The density of the water is $1.0 \times 10^{3}\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}^{-3}$. The difference between the pressures on the top
and bottom faces of the cylinder is 520 Pa.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the height h of the cylinder.
h = m
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the height h of the cylinder.
$h = m $

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.question_text: Show that the upthrust acting on the cylinder is 0.39 N.
parts.question_text_latex: Show that the upthrust acting on the cylinder is 0.39 N.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the tension T in the string.
T = N
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the tension T in the string.
$T = N $

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
The string is now used to move the cylinder in (a) vertically upwards through the water. The
variation with time t of the velocity v of the cylinder is shown in Fig. 2.2.
parts.question_text_latex:
The string is now used to move the cylinder in (a) vertically upwards through the water. The
variation with time t of the velocity v of the cylinder is shown in Fig. 2.2.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.question_text:
Use Fig. 2.2 to determine the acceleration of the cylinder at time t = 2.0 s.
acceleration = m s ^{2}
parts.question_text_latex:
Use Fig. 2.2 to determine the acceleration of the cylinder at time t = 2.0 s.
$acceleration = m s ^{2} $

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.question_text:
The top face of the cylinder is at a depth of 0.32 m below the surface of the water at time
t = 0.
Use Fig. 2.2 to determine the depth of the top face below the surface of the water at time
t = 4.0 s.
depth = m
parts.question_text_latex:
The top face of the cylinder is at a depth of 0.32 m below the surface of the water at time
$t = 0.$
Use Fig. 2.2 to determine the depth of the top face below the surface of the water at time
$t = 4.0 s.$
$depth = m $

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
The cylinder in (b) is released from the string at time t = 4.0 s. The cylinder falls, from rest,
vertically downwards through the water. Assume that the upthrust acting on the cylinder
remains constant as it falls.
parts.question_text_latex:

vertically downwards through the water. Assume that the upthrust acting on the cylinder
remains constant as it falls.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.question_text:
State the name of the force that acts on the cylinder when it is moving and does not act
on the cylinder when it is stationary.
parts.question_text_latex:
State the name of the force that acts on the cylinder when it is moving and does not act
on the cylinder when it is stationary.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.question_text:
State and explain the variation, if any, of the acceleration of the cylinder as it falls
downwards through the water.

downwards through the water.
